newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police tear gas demonstrators.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police tear gas demonstrators.

text.p: Police fired tear gas to break up a street battle in Jakarta on Tuesday between supporters of rival parties in Indonesia's general election campaign, witnesses said.

They said about 200 supporters of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP), armed with machetes and knives, clashed with loyalists of the ruling Golkar party in an eastern suburb of Jakarta. There were no immediate reports of casualties.

Witnesses said the Golkar supporters pelted their rivals with stones. The PPP earlier said it would not campaign in the capital of 10 million people on Tuesday following two days of violence between its supporters and Golkar last weekend.
The PPP, Golkar, and the badly-split Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are the only parties legally permitted to contest May 29 general elections which the ruling party is expected to win easily.

The three parties had a pre-election agreement to campaign in separate parts of the country each day to avoid violent confrontations. Tuesday was the PPP day to campaign in Java. Most of the violence centred on central and western Java, including Jakarta, has been between PPP and Golkar supporters.
The campaign officially ends on Friday to provide a cooling off period before the country's 125 million eligible voters go to the polls.
